text: It's four o'clock already. I hate to leave, but I think I must. Can you stay a little longer?

text: Yes. That would be nice. When do you want to go? Is today OK?

text: My shirt needs ironing. Could you please help me with that, Mary? No way. Do it yourself.

text: Waiter, can I have the bill please? Wait a moment. It's $ 30.

request_text: Amy, could you help me with this work?
response_text: Sorry, I'm busy. Why don't you ask Alice?

text: Can you speed up a bit? Sorry. The road is too crowded.
request_text: Can you speed up a bit?
response_text: Sorry. The road is too crowded.

text: Alice, it really was great. I think it was the most interesting thing here. You really should go in. No, I don't want to.

response_text: No, I don't want to.

text: May I invite you for a dance? With pleasure.
request_text: May I invite you for a dance?

text: Excuse me, would you like to be our guide? Of course.
request_text: Excuse me, would you like to be our guide?

text: Why don't you have dinner with me tonight? I'd love to.
request_text: Why don't you have dinner with me tonight?

text: I know there is a beautiful farm in the countryside near Taipei. Are you interested in going there? why not? I love animals and I love nature.

text: Hey, if you're not busy this weekend, would you like to go see a movie? Sounds good. What should we see?

response_text: Sounds good. What should we see?

text: Actually, I haven ’ t had time to look it over. Did you bring another copy with you? Of course, here you are, sir.

text: Do you mind washing my clothes? Not at all. It's no problem.

response_text: Not at all. It's no problem.
notes: Negative-polar request (Do you mind) granted via Not-at-all -- a grant whose surface polarity is negative, a genuine polarity-composition test akin to the McGuffey-era litotes item it replaces.

text: May I sit here? I'm afraid this seat is taken.
request_text: May I sit here?

text: I'd like to make an appointment with manager Mr.Wu. Would 10:00 a. m. tomorrow be all right? I'm afraid not. He has a meeting tomorrow morning.

response_text: I'm afraid not. He has a meeting tomorrow morning.

text: I won't do it again. Please forgive me. No way. I've given you too many chances already.

response_text: No way. I've given you too many chances already.

text: Am I allowed to eat spicy food? I'm afraid not.
request_text: Am I allowed to eat spicy food?
response_text: I'm afraid not.

text: Welcome to Lincoln Bank. What can I help you with, Sir? I'm not sure if I'm at the right counter, but I need some advice on mortgages, can you help me?

text: Is 5 PM. Saturday a good time for you? Hmm, how about seven? I can treat you to dinner. Sure, that would be great. I'll bring the wine. OK. Then I'll be expecting you.
request_text: Sure, that would be great. I'll bring the wine.
response_text: OK. Then I'll be expecting you.
notes: CONCESSION: initial time proposal (5PM) is met with a counter-proposal (7PM plus dinner) rather than an immediate answer; requester accepts the counter-proposal, responder then confirms. request_text/response_text = the final renegotiated ask plus its confirming grant (same convention as the McGuffey-era concession items this replaces).

Thanks for inviting me.

text: Well, don't worry about dinner. I'll only make vegetarian dishes for you. Do you like sushi? I prefer cooked fish to raw fish, but if you really like it, make it. How about a spicy tofu and vegetable stir-fry? That sounds great. What time should I come over?

text: What about sunday? I wish I could, but it's my mums birthday. Maybe next week. Much as I'd like to, I am afraid i wont be free next week, I have a lot of work.

text: We'd like to invite you for our dress party tomorrow evening, are you free? Much as we'd like to, but we've booked up already for that time. What a pity! You can't join us. So sorry. Next time we'll go, thanks anyway.

text: You need a babysitter. Yes, I'd ask Jill, the girl I've had before, but I need someone overnight.Maybe even for two nights. I could have Suzy stay at my place. I don't want to do that to you, Karen.
